title: A Thorn for the Sigil
premise: Freya Reyes, a runaway hedge-witch's apprentice who knows every smuggler's road through the Thornfell mountains, takes in a mute child who speaks a language older than any kingdom. The child is the last vessel of a soul sold generations ago to the Sigil Court beneath the mountain, and the court's tithe-collectors have come to reclaim it before the long winter seals the passes. Freya, the child, and a disgraced tithe-collector named Ashen descend into the court to steal the soul back, discovering that Freya's own master sold her name as collateral years ago. In the climax, Freya trades her stolen name for the child's soul, breaking the court's ledger; she survives nameless but free, and the found family they've gathered carries her home through the first snow.
about_author: Lior Fairweather is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, magical, and emotional—from a cabin full of unreliable clocks.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Left
chapters.summary: Freya Reyes, POV. Three years after fleeing her master Maren's cottage, Freya smuggles charms along the Thornfell roads, trading on knowledge she was never meant to keep. A letter arrives bearing Maren's seal—and Freya burns it unopened. The beat is restless independence shadowed by guilt over what she abandoned.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dark
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. During an early blizzard, a small child appears at her door, frostbitten and silent, speaking words no local tongue matches. When Freya touches the child's hand, she glimpses a vast hall beneath stone. The beat is wary compassion—the first crack in Freya's self-imposed solitude.

chapters.title: What the Old Tongue Says
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya seeks out Brother Callum, a defrocked monk who collects dead languages. He translates one phrase: 'the debt comes due at first snow.' Outside, figures in grey robes begin asking questions in every village. The beat is dawning dread as the child becomes a target.

chapters.title: Grey Robes at the Ford
chapters.summary: Ashen, POV (introduced). A tithe-collector of the Sigil Court tracks the escaped vessel, bound by oath to retrieve what the mountain owns. Ashen hesitates at the ford, remembering another child collected long ago. The beat is duty strained by buried doubt.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya flees into the high passes with the child—whom she names Wren—using smuggler trails only she knows. They shelter with Ostara, a one-armed bear-trainer who owes Freya a life-debt. The beat is found family forming under pressure, warmth against cold.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Forced to revisit her old master's cottage for supplies, Freya finds Maren dying and a ledger listing names sold to the court—including, in faded ink, 'Reyes, Freya.' Maren confesses she sold Freya's name to pay a cure for the plague. The beat is betrayal and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Grieving and furious, Freya realizes why the court's magic has always felt familiar: part of her already belongs beneath the mountain. Wren comforts her wordlessly, sharing visions of the court's halls. The beat is grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ashen Catches Up
chapters.summary: Ashen, POV. Ashen corners them at Ostara's cabin but cannot complete the taking when Wren looks at him without fear. He defects instead, revealing the court plans to consume Wren's soul to extend the long winter indefinitely. The beat is an enemy becoming an uneasy ally.

chapters.title: Ostara's Stand
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Grey-robes assault the cabin; Ostara and her bears hold the pass so the others can escape through a cave system. Ostara falls behind, buying time with blood. The beat is sacrifice—the first true cost of the journey.

chapters.title: Under the Mountain's Skin
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. The three travel the deep roads: rivers that flow upward, forests of mineral trees, echoes of everyone the court has taken. Wren grows stronger the deeper they go, which frightens Freya. The beat is wonder curdling into claustrophobia.

chapters.title: The Tithe-Taker's Confession
chapters.summary: Ashen, POV. Around a fire of cold flame, Ashen tells how he was collected as a boy and remade as a collector, his own name struck from the world. Freya recognizes her possible future in him. The beat is empathy across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Gate of Names
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. To enter the court proper, each traveler must surrender a memory at the gate. Freya gives up her memory of Maren's kindness; Ashen gives his mother's face. The beat is quiet horror—entry purchased with pieces of the self.

chapters.title: The Sigil Court
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Beneath the mountain glitters a court of the nameless, beautiful and hollow, ruled by the Auditor, a being of pure accounting. Wren's soul sits in the treasury as a glowing sigil-stone. The beat is awe and revulsion entwined.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Auditor
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. The Auditor offers Freya a bargain: her name restored, her debts forgiven, if she delivers Wren willingly. It shows her the comfortable life she could have had. The beat is temptation aimed precisely at her oldest wound.

chapters.title: The Treasury of Souls
chapters.summary: Ashen, POV. While Freya stalls the Auditor, Ashen uses his collector's credentials to reach the treasury, finding thousands of sigil-stones—including, he realizes, his own. The beat is vertigo and courage as he chooses theft over obedience.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Cornered by guards, Wren breaks their silence at last—in the old tongue, commanding stone and shadow. The child is not merely a vessel but the last heir of the people the court consumed. The beat is revelation: the hunted one is the rightful claimant.

chapters.title: Ledger-Breaking
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. In the climax's opening move, Freya seizes the master ledger and offers the trade the Auditor cannot refuse under court law: her name, freely given, for Wren's soul. The Auditor accepts, bound by its own rules. The beat is self-sacrifice as strategy and love.

chapters.title: The Mountain Wakes
chapters.summary: Ashen, POV. Wren's returned soul ignites the old tongue throughout the court; the nameless begin remembering themselves, and the structure rebels against the Auditor. Ashen reclaims his own name from the treasury amid collapse. The beat is cathartic uprising.

chapters.title: Running Before the Winter Seals
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Nameless now and fading at the edges, Freya must be led out by Wren and Ashen through collapsing deep roads as winter storms close the passes above. She cannot remember why she is running, only whom she refuses to let go. The beat is terror and devotion stripped of identity.

chapters.title: What a Name Is Worth
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Above ground, Wren works the old tongue one final time—not restoring Freya's sold name, but weaving her a new one from the family they've become. Freya remembers herself, changed. The beat is rebirth: identity as chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: First Snow, Last Debt
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. They bury Ostara's token at the pass, and Ashen—name restored—chooses to stay in Thornfell rather than return to a court that no longer exists. Wren begins learning the common tongue, teaching the old one in exchange. The beat is mourning braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Spring: Freya reopens Maren's cottage as a school for hedge-craft and forgotten languages, Wren her first student, travelers and strays filling its rooms. On the doorstep, a new knock—a stranger fleeing something old. Freya opens the door. The beat is the found family becoming a refuge, the cycle turned to grace.
